Vardø|Norway.f: This is the easternmost town in Norway, at 31 degrees east, farther east than Saint Petersburg, Kyiv and Istanbul.

Grímsey|Iceland.f: The Arctic Circle is shifting north about 14.5 metres a year and is due to leave the island around 2047.

Berlevåg|Norway.f: The village was completely burned down in November 1944 and its people forcibly evacuated in the German scorched earth strategy.

Båtsfjord|Norway.f: The world's northernmost gannet colony is on a sea stack at Syltefjordstauran, grown from two pairs found in 1961 to over 300.

Vadsø|Norway.f: The airship mast on Vadsoya was used by Nobile and Amundsen for their 1926 flight over the North Pole in the Norge.

Elba|Italy.f: Elba is the largest island of the Tuscan Archipelago and the site of Napoleon's first exile, from 1814 to 1815.

Svolvær|Norway.f: Svolvaergeita, the town's most famous mountain, had its first recorded climb in 1910.

Stokmarknes|Norway.f: Hurtigruten's headquarters and the Coastal Express Museum are here, though the settlement only got town status in 2000.

Vopnafjörður|Iceland.f: Vopnafjordur was the largest port of Icelandic emigration to America in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

Honningsvåg|Norway.f: The dog Bamse, mascot of the Free Norwegian Forces in the Second World War, came from here.

Mehamn|Norway.f: In 1903 fishermen destroyed Mehamn's whaling station, believing the whales drove fish toward the shore.

Leknes|Norway.f: At Leknes the midnight sun stays above the horizon from May 26 to July 17.

Alderney|Guernsey.f: About a quarter of Alderney's hedgehogs are the white or blonde variety, which does not carry fleas.

Mo i Rana|Norway.f: Mo i Rana sits about 30 km south of the Arctic Circle and produced its first steel in 1955.
